## Context of the Data handling project  

- Introduction to programming for economics students (3rd semester)  
- Relevance of data science skills in today’s world  
- Data pipeline basics: importing, cleaning, transforming, visualizing 

  ![](images/data_science_pipeline.png){width="50%"}
  
  



## Data visualization - Tools
<span style="color:#7f8c8d;">ggplot2</span>

- **Layers** (build plots step by step)  
- **Geoms** (visual representation: points, lines, bars)  
- **Aesthetics** (mapping data to visual properties)  
- **Facets** (split data into subplots)  

## Data visualization - Tools
<span style="color:#7f8c8d;">gtExtras</span>

- Extension to the gt package for enhanced tables  
- Adds visual elements (bars, icons, color scales)  
- Makes tables more informative and easier to read  



## Data visualization – Principles

<span style="color:#7f8c8d;">Encoding of values</span>

- Position relative to axes (line, scatter)
- Size of area (bar, area)
- Continuous vs. categorical → choose appropriate chart

---

## Data visualization – Principles

<span style="color:#7f8c8d;">Clarity and integrity</span>

- Avoid misleading representations (Lie factor)
- Maximize data-to-ink ratio
- Maintain appropriate data density

---

## Data visualization – Principles

<span style="color:#7f8c8d;">Communication</span>

- Fit the whole story into one graph (if possible)
- Graph should be understandable without explanation

---

## Data visualization – Principles

<span style="color:#7f8c8d;">Simplicity</span>

- Avoid unnecessary visual elements
- Avoid pie charts and 3D charts
